oil.when: 2020–2026 Durango with push-button start (cluster menu method)
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed.
Without touching the brake pedal, press ENGINE START/STOP once so the ignition is in ON/RUN. Do not start the engine.
Press the down arrow on the steering wheel until Vehicle Info shows in the cluster.
Press the right arrow to open the Oil Life screen.
Press and hold OK until the oil life reads 100%.
Press the up arrow to leave the screen. If a message says the engine must be off with the ignition in run, set the ignition that way and try again.
oil.note: Checked in the 2020, 2021 and 2026 owner's manuals.

oil.when: 2020–2026 Durango with push-button start, backup method if the menu reset does not work (accelerator pedal)
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed.
Without touching the brake pedal, press ENGINE START/STOP once so the ignition is in ON/RUN. Do not start the engine.
Slowly push the accelerator pedal all the way down and let it up, three times, all within about 10 seconds.
Without touching the brake, press ENGINE START/STOP once to turn the ignition off.
Start the engine. If the oil change message comes back, the reset did not take, so repeat the steps.
oil.note: Checked in the 2020 and 2026 owner's manuals.

tpms.when: 2012–2026 Durango (no reset button; the light clears itself)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker, using your own gauge.
Drive normally. The system reads the new pressures by itself, which can take up to about 20 minutes of driving above 15 mph.
The light goes out once the system has the corrected pressures. There is no button or menu reset.
tpms.note: If the light flashes for about 75 seconds at start-up and then stays on, that is a system fault (such as a failed sensor), not low air, and only a repair clears it. Checked in the 2012 and 2026 owner's manuals.
